title: Drift Wood · the Spring Special
logline: The estuary at low tide. Wood's first landscape. Captioned — the last one he'll caption.

panels.composition: A full-page drawing for the paper's spring issue. The Alsea estuary at low tide from the bluff: mudflats in long hatched bands, a channel of water catching a white sky, pilings of the old cannery dock, a heron, log booms, the far shore's spruce wall. Over-inked, ambitious, everything crosshatched. At the bottom, a hand-lettered caption explaining what the reader is looking at.
panels.caption: THE ESTUARY AT LOW TIDE. Everything that leaves this town goes out through here. Most of it comes back. — A.F.

image.prompt: a full-page black-and-white pen drawing of a Pacific Northwest estuary at low tide seen from a bluff: long bands of crosshatched mudflats, a channel of water reflecting a white sky, old cannery dock pilings, a heron, log booms, a far wall of spruce, over-inked and ambitious, xerox grain
image.notes: The caption is part of the page; letter it after if needed. It's the only captioned landscape in thirty years.

notes: The last landscape he explains. Every later one is silent.
